Penyige Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Penyige, Hungary

Not demolished. Penyige's Jewish cemetery is dated by its oldest surviving tombstone to 1874, with its latest dated 1924. The Jewish population numbered 26 in the 1840 census, peaked at 36 in 1880 (out of 595 total residents), then declined to 32 by 1910, 17 by 1920, and 12 by 1930; by 1941 it stood at 20 out of 816 residents. Penyige's Jews were first confined to the Fehérgyarmat Ghetto, then deported from the Mátészalka Ghetto to Auschwitz on May 31, 1944. The village's synagogue was later demolished, but its fenced cemetery has survived in good condition despite being abandoned.
